What will President Trump's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz do to energy prices and the global economy? I asked @ProfessorKaren of @ColumbiaUEnergy:

Video

How has the war with Iran impacted relations between the United States and its Gulf Arab allies? I spoke with the director of @MiddleEast_HKS, Tarek Masoud.

Video

Former Secretary of State @ABlinken told me why President Biden did not rejoin the Iran nuclear deal after President Trump withdrew during his first term. Part 2 of our conversation:

Video

This morning JD Vance and his delegation departed Islamabad, Pakistan, after 21 hours of talks with the Iranians failed to secure a peace deal. What is negotiating with the Iranians actually like? I sat down on Thursday with former Secretary of State @ABlinken, who helped steer policy on Iran under both the Biden and Obama administrations:

Video

President Trump announced this morning the US would blockade the Strait of Hormuz. How would this actually happen? I asked retired Admiral @stavridisj, the former NATO supreme allied commander.

Video

For most of America's history, freedom of navigation has been treated not as a privilege to be sold, but as a right to be defended.

To abandon that now in the Strait of Hormuz, as President Trump has suggested, is to trade a durable advantage for a fleeting gain.

My take:

Video

Tarek Masoud of @MiddleEast_HKS how US allies in the Gulf are reacting & @ProfessorKaren of @ColumbiaUEnergy what it means for energy markets. But the U.S. benefits most not from charging per ship for access, but from building a world in which commerce flows freely.
